mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions for corporations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: In the specified trigger regime, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) or the 5-day moving average of SPX returns remains non-negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as labor market strength supports corporate earnings optimism.
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the average 20-day forward return is negative or the 95% confidence interval includes zero.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 2.0% in the following month, the S&P 500 forward 5-day return is expected to be negative due to market anticipation of tighter monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL surprises above +2.0% in the next month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the S&P 500 5-day average is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in the next month, followed by a rebound of at least 3% in the subsequent month, predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over 20 days as a potential bottom in supply chain disruptions is signaled.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -5% in month 1 and rises > +3% in month 2
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return after the pattern is detected (p > 0.05) or the pattern does not precede a positive return in at least 60% of occurrences.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of falling residential housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be positive as the housing cycle weakness reduces risk aversion and supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 20-day window, forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the S&P 500 5-day average remains negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for two consecutive months, accompanied by rising retail sales (PAYEMS), predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over 60 days as labor market tightness supports economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for two consecutive months AND PAYEMS rising
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with robust payrolls
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: Unexpectedly strong retail activity (RSAFS) exceeding 400,000 thousand dollars in a month, when previous month was below 350,000, predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as the market anticipates overheating demand and potential corrections.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the S&P 500 5-day average is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in industrial production (INDPRO) — a sharp decline followed by a smaller rebound within the same month — predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over 20 days as market participants interpret this as ongoing supply disruptions.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -4% in the month and rebounds by < +2% in the same month
failure_condition: In the specified trigger regime, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) or the pattern is not associated with negative returns in at least 70% of occurrences.
